newsitem.title: USA: BPA limits Friday peak power offer to 300 MW.
newsitem.headline: BPA limits Friday peak power offer to 300 MW.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) limited its sales of non-firm power during "valley peaks" on Friday to 300 megawatts (MW), compared with 500 MW for the previous day, the agency said Thursday.
BPA left prices for non-firm power during hours ending 1200-1800 PDT and 2200 PDT at $15.00 per MWh for Northwest deliveriesand $16.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) deliveries.
The agency continued to refrain from offering surplus power during morning and evening peaks.
Prices for non-firm power for hours ending at 0600 PDT and 2300 PDT were unchanged at $10.00 for all deliveries.
Prices for off-peak non-firm power during hours ending 0100-0500 PDT and 2400 PDT were also flat at $9.50.
Firm power during off-peak hours on Friday was unchanged at at $9.50.
